o: Deleting rightmost characters means the final common string must be a prefix of all three strings. So find the longest common prefix length L; if L = 0 it is impossible (-1), otherwise the operation count is (len(s1)-L)+(len(s2)-L)+(len(s3)-L). Example 1: prefix "ab", L=2, deletions 1+1+0=2. Example 2: first characters differ, L=0, answer -1.
k: Only prefixes survive deletion, so the target string is exactly the common prefix.
Feasible iff the first characters of all three strings match.
Answer = total length minus 3 times the common-prefix length.

a.i: Compare characters position by position across the three strings until a mismatch or a string ends; count matched positions L and compute total lengths minus 3L.
s: Loop i while i < min length and s1[i]==s2[i]==s3[i], incrementing L.

w: Strings cannot be emptied, hence the L = 0 impossibility check. Note the target may be shorter than some string's full length — that is fine, we just trim. Follow-up: k strings instead of 3 (same logic generalizes), or minimum operations if arbitrary-character deletion were allowed.
